knowledge_base: LTE DL Throughput Degradation -- Recommended Solutions
id_scheme: Each solution's id matches a subcategory parent_id in causes.json. Actions with no 'applies_if' always show. Actions with 'applies_if' only show if that specific supporting-evidence id also matched.

recommended_actions.action: Run a capacity audit on the specific eNodeBs where true congestion concentrates.
Check PRB scheduler fairness/weights and consider Mobility Load Balancing (MLB) toward underutilized neighbor cells.
This co-occurs with Low Rank -- check C10 (MIMO Rank Fallback) before committing to a pure capacity fix.
This co-occurs with No CA -- check C13 (CA Inactive) before committing to a pure capacity fix.
Prioritize capacity expansion (new carrier, small cell) over scheduler tuning -- this cell is genuinely out of room.
Low operational bandwidth is the bottleneck -- evaluate a bandwidth upgrade or refarming before any scheduler tuning.

standards_and_vendor_references.source: 3GPP SON framework (Mobility Load Balancing use case)
standards_and_vendor_references.note: MLB is one of the standard 3GPP SON functions for redistributing load between cells to relieve congestion.
An 80% PRB-utilization breakpoint is commonly used as the point above which a cell is considered congested.

recommended_actions.action: Investigate scheduler configuration (proportional-fair weights, QCI/5QI prioritization) at the affected cells rather than assuming a capacity ceiling.
Confirm CQI/MCS reporting is not being under-utilized due to an overly conservative outer-loop link-adaptation offset.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: Defines how reported CQI maps to MCS selection, the basis for checking whether the scheduler is under-using an available link quality.

recommended_actions.action: Site/antenna audit: check tilt, azimuth, and transmit power at the serving site.
Consider a new site, small cell, or repeater if the coverage hole is confirmed across multiple drive passes.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: Defines the RSRP/RSRQ measurement basis used to quantify and act on weak-coverage conditions.
Below -110 dBm RSRP is treated as weak coverage in this project's threshold table.

recommended_actions.action: RF/interference hunt on the specific eNodeB (check for external interferers, PIM, or uncoordinated small-cell deployments).
Verify this isn't actually a coverage issue misclassified as interference -- confirm RSRP genuinely sits above -110 dBm on repeated passes before committing budget to an interference hunt.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: Defines the RSRQ/SINR measurements used to distinguish interference from weak coverage.
Good RSRP with degraded SINR is explicitly identified as an interference signature, not a coverage issue.

recommended_actions.action: Check OSS alarms/counters for the serving site during this exact time window -- Radio Link Failure with normal own-radio conditions is the classic signature of a site/hardware fault, not an RF problem.
Review Mobility Robustness Optimization (MRO) counters for too-late or too-early handover contributing to this failure type.
No RF tuning action is appropriate here until an outage/alarm event is confirmed or ruled out.

standards_and_vendor_references.source: 3GPP TS 36.331 clause 5.3.11.3 (RLF), cross-referenced with SON Mobility Robustness Optimization
standards_and_vendor_references.note: RLF with normal radio conditions at failure time is a classic MRO/hardware-fault diagnostic signature, not an RF issue.

recommended_actions.action: Check OSS alarms/counters for both the serving site AND its immediate neighbors during this exact time window -- this pattern (throughput/session collapse with no radio explanation) cannot on its own tell you which site is at fault.
Cross-reference against site maintenance, reset, or transport-link logs for the same window before dispatching an RF team.

If Serving Cell RB Utilization Increase is present, check this cell's own capacity was adequate for the observed load before assuming a neighbor failure -- rising utilization alone doesn't confirm a neighbor went down.
If Neighbor Cell Availability Drop is present, prioritize checking that specific neighbor's OSS status first -- but treat this as a lead to investigate, not a confirmed cause.
No RF tuning action is appropriate here until an outage/alarm event is confirmed or ruled out on either site.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: Standard practice is to correlate a throughput/traffic collapse signature against OSS alarms before pursuing an RF explanation -- and to check neighboring sites, not just the serving cell, before attributing fault.

recommended_actions.action: Increase both Event A3 hysteresis and Time-to-Trigger (TTT) at the affected boundary -- an increase from TTT=100ms to TTT=320ms with A3 offset/hysteresis raised from 2dB to 4dB has been shown to stabilize ping-pong behavior.
This is a recurring site-level pattern across multiple episodes -- run an ANR (Automatic Neighbor Relation) audit at this eNodeB rather than tuning a single boundary.
Increase Event A3 hysteresis/offset or reduce TTT at this boundary; this is a one-off so far, not yet a confirmed site-level pattern.
Investigate target-cell admission handling -- the handover attempt itself was rejected/unprepared, a different fault than a timing/threshold issue.
Consider a speed-dependent handover parameter set (faster TTT/lower hysteresis) rather than treating this as a stationary-UE tuning problem.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: The standard parameter family governing handover sensitivity; the same three parameters trade off ping-pong, late-HO, and early-HO risk against each other.
Specifies the management requirements for Automatic Neighbor Relations, the standard mechanism for diagnosing a persistent wrong-neighbor-relation pattern.

recommended_actions.action: Check RACH configuration (preamble format, power ramping step, max preamble transmissions) at the affected cells.
Investigate uplink coverage/interference at the affected site if RACH access delay is elevated.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: 3GPP defines RACH parameter self-optimization as a standard SON function to reduce access/handoff time and RACH failures.

recommended_actions.action: Antenna/RF-path check at the concentrated eNodeBs: verify cross-polarization discrimination and antenna spacing/correlation.
Check UE-side MIMO capability/reporting if the pattern is UE-specific rather than site-specific.

standards_and_vendor_references.source: 3GPP TS 36.213 (Rank Indication reporting, closed-loop spatial multiplexing)
standards_and_vendor_references.note: Defines how the UE derives and reports Rank Indication (RI), the basis for confirming a persistent Rank-1 report is a genuine link-adaptation output rather than a reporting error.

recommended_actions.action: RF/coverage check specifically on the secondary carrier's frequency/band at the affected site.
Do not disable CA as a fix -- the issue is the secondary carrier's radio quality, not CA logic itself.
SCell is being scheduled almost nothing despite being active -- check scheduler weighting on the secondary carrier before assuming a pure RF cause.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: Confirms SCell activation is a MAC-layer procedure separate from RF quality -- supporting that a weak-secondary-cell fault sits in the RF domain, not the CA control logic.

recommended_actions.action: Investigate why the SCell deactivation timer (sCellDeactivationTimer) is expiring or being triggered mid-episode.
High SCell BLER preceded the release -- treat this as a C11 (Weak Secondary Cell) RF problem first; the release may be a correct network response, not the root fault.
SCell CQI was also degraded before release -- corroborates a radio-quality-driven release; prioritize the RF check over scheduler/timer tuning.

standards_and_vendor_references.note: Specifies that the UE deactivates an SCell either on receipt of a deactivation MAC CE or automatically upon sCellDeactivationTimer expiry.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm the UE/device is CA-capable and a secondary carrier is actually deployed/in-range at this location before treating this as a fault.
Check CA feature licensing/activation at the site and CA-capability flags in the UE context.
Investigate outer-loop link adaptation (OLLA) tuning at the affected cells if BLER sits persistently away from the ~10% target band regardless of SINR/MCS.
Treat this as a lower-priority bucket relative to Congestion/Coverage/Interference -- revisit after those are addressed, since it often shrinks once upstream causes are fixed.

standards_and_vendor_references.source: 3GPP TS 36.213-aligned CQI design assumption and industry OLLA practice
standards_and_vendor_references.note: CQI reporting assumes a ~10% initial-transmission BLER target; Outer-Loop Link Adaptation adjusts the SINR-to-CQI offset to converge BLER toward that target.

recommended_actions.action: No action needed -- confirm this bucket stays excluded from all root-cause totals and dashboards, since these are idle-radio or unclassifiable samples, not confirmed network faults.
